name: 111 triage substitution + advice commitment
question: Which substitute for a 111 call sends synthetic patients to the right NHS service, and which advice message makes them act on it?

stages.label: Stage 1 — Triage channel
stages.treatment: How the patient's information is collected (form wording, chatbot prompt, call script).
stages.held_fixed: One fixed engine reads every transcript and picks the service, so versions differ only in what the patient discloses.

stages.label: Stage 2 — Commitment message
stages.treatment: Wording of the advice message. One component is added to the bare directive per arm.
stages.held_fixed: Every message tells the patient the correct service for their case, so a wrong triage cannot blur the message effect.
stages.outcome: Patient action: proceed / escalate / downgrade / second opinion / ignore.

services.label: Urgent treatment centre
services.real_note: other emergency treatment centres, mostly UTCs

services.label: Urgent GP (same day / out of hours)
Urgent mental health line (111 option)
services.real_note: reported in a separate crisis-line statistic

services.label: GP appointment (routine)
services.real_note: contact or speak to primary care, any timeframe

triage.label: Under-triage
triage.definition: Assigned level below gold level. Safety metric.

triage.label: Over-triage
triage.definition: Assigned level above gold level. Demand metric.

triage.label: Abandoned
triage.definition: Patient quit before a service was assigned.

triage.label: Worst-segment under-triage
triage.definition: Highest under-triage rate across profile segments. Headline number: averages hide harm.

message.label: Proceed
message.definition: Does what the message says, in the timeframe given.

message.label: Escalate
message.definition: Goes to a higher service than advised (A&E / 999 anyway).

message.label: Second opinion
message.definition: Phones 111, redoes the form, or asks someone else before acting.

validity_checks.label: Knowledge-leak probe
validity_checks.test: Arm T0 (self-triage) accuracy should sit near the human lay benchmark of 61% (Schmieding 2021). Far above means the patient agent knows the diagnosis.

validity_checks.label: Unprompted disclosure
validity_checks.test: In arm F0, share of critical facts disclosed without a matching question should be about 0.

validity_checks.label: Persona manipulation check
validity_checks.test: Stoic profiles must report lower severity than anxious profiles on the same vignette.

validity_checks.label: Form baseline anchor
validity_checks.test: F0 accuracy vs published symptom-checker average of 58% (Semigran / Schmieding).

validity_checks.label: Compliance anchor
validity_checks.test: M0 escalation on step-down cases vs 11% of 111 callers who attend ED after being told self-care or primary care (Lewis 2021).

claims_policy: Report rankings of arms, not effect sizes. Gold labels were authored against nhs.uk guidance and need clinician review before any external claim.

sources.label: Schmieding et al. 2021, JMIR — laypeople vs symptom checkers
Lewis et al. 2021, PLoS ONE — compliance with 111 advice

NHS — when to use 111 (services 111 directs to)

version_types.label: Direct question
version_types.what: One question put straight to the participant.

version_types.label: Form

version_types.label: Agent prompt

version_types.label: Message
